newsitem.title: USA: Yeltsin revels in spotlight at G7 summit.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin revels in spotlight at G7 summit.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, revelling in his early successes at a Group of Seven summit, blew kisses and plunged unexpectedly into an adoring crowd on Friday to meet the people of Denver.
"Denver is good," Yeltsin said, grinning broadly and giving the thumbs-up sign as he shook hands with members of a crowd of about 200 people after leaving talks with U.S. President Bill Clinton.
The crowd chanted "Yeltsin, Yeltsin," when he suddenly turned and headed in their direction instead of getting into his limousine.

The 66-year-old president, who also blew kisses to a small crowd on the way into his talks with Clinton, looked fit and energetic four months after returning to the Kremlin following heart problems and then pneumonia.
Yeltsin had plenty to celebrate. He and Clinton announced agreement for Russia to join the Paris Club of creditor nations, who meet to discuss requests to renegotiate nations'debts.
"I just received some good news, so I'm in a good mood," Yeltsin told reporters.

Earlier at talks with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, he pledged to stop targeting Japan with nuclear missiles and said it was time for Russia to "de-target" China, according to Japanese officials.
Russia is enjoying its biggest ever role at summits of the Group of Seven industrialised nations and Yeltsin is pushing to be admitted as a full member of the exclusive club.
